# MongoDB query shape optimization — facts

## Sort and pagination

- [fact] With a sort, $in under 201 elements expands and merges via a SORT_MERGE stage; at 201 or more it behaves like a range and blocks index sorting on later keys. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in/
- [fact] skip() walks and discards index keys or documents on every page; keyset pagination filters on the last seen sort key instead. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip/
- [fact] A blocking sort holds the whole result in memory up to 100 MB per stage and spills to disk when allowDiskUse is enabled. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort/
MongoDB query shape optimization — facts > Operators

## Operators

- [fact] An unanchored $regex scans every index key; only a case-sensitive pattern with a ^ prefix gets tight index bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex/
- [fact] $ne and $nin also match documents missing the field and cannot use selective index bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne/
- [fact] $where runs JavaScript per document, cannot use an index and is deprecated from MongoDB 8.0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where/

Shard a collection > Steps

# Shard a collection

## Steps

1. Choose a shard key with high cardinality and non-monotonic values.
2. Create an index that starts with the shard key.
3. Run sh.shardCollection("db.coll", { key: 1 }) and watch the balancer distribute chunks.
## Verify

Run db.coll.getShardDistribution() and confirm every shard holds data.
MongoDB Atlas > Private Endpoints

# MongoDB Atlas

## Private Endpoints

Atlas private endpoints use AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link or GCP Private Service Connect so that
application traffic never crosses the public internet. Each endpoint is regional.
MongoDB Atlas > Atlas Vector Search

## Atlas Vector Search

$vectorSearch runs an approximate nearest-neighbour search. numCandidates controls recall versus
latency; a value of 10 to 20 times the limit is a common starting point. Pre-filter fields must be
indexed as filter fields in the vector index definition.
MongoDB Atlas > Performance Advisor

## Performance Advisor

The Performance Advisor ranks slow query shapes and suggests indexes by impact. Treat each suggestion
as evidence and confirm it with explain().
MongoDB Indexes > Compound Indexes and the ESR Rule

# MongoDB Indexes

## Compound Indexes and the ESR Rule

A compound index orders keys by Equality, then Sort, then Range. When the sort keys follow the
equality keys, MongoDB returns documents in index order and avoids a blocking in-memory sort.
Indexing the range field before the sort field forces a SORT stage.
MongoDB Indexes > Multikey Indexes

## Multikey Indexes

An index on an array field is multikey: one index key per array element. Bounds on multikey
fields can only be intersected when the predicates sit inside one $elemMatch.
MongoDB Indexes > Partial and Sparse Indexes

## Partial and Sparse Indexes

A partial index stores only documents that match its partialFilterExpression. The planner uses it
only when the query predicate implies that expression. Sparse indexes skip documents that lack the field.
MongoDB Indexes > Hidden Indexes

## Hidden Indexes

Hide an index with hideIndex() before dropping it. A hidden index is still maintained on writes
but the planner ignores it, so unhiding it is instant.
Sharding > Choosing a Shard Key

# Sharding

## Choosing a Shard Key

A good shard key has high cardinality, low frequency and non-monotonic values. A monotonically
increasing shard key such as a timestamp sends every insert to one chunk: a hot shard.
Sharding > Chunk Migration and the Balancer

## Chunk Migration and the Balancer

The balancer moves chunks between shards in the balancing window. Jumbo chunks exceed the chunk size
and cannot be split because every document shares one shard key value.
Sharding > Targeted and Scatter-Gather Queries

## Targeted and Scatter-Gather Queries

A query that includes the shard key is routed to one shard (SINGLE_SHARD). Without it, mongos sends
the query to every shard and merges the results (SHARD_MERGE), which is a scatter-gather query.
